candidates.title: Inside Prometheus: Meta's Journey to a Gigawatt-Scale Supercluster
candidates.why: Meta's own engineers on what it takes to turn an ordinary data centre into a gigawatt training cluster in two years: 800G networking per GPU, fabrics of 20,736 GPUs spanning sites up to 100+ km apart, 120-170 kW liquid-cooled racks, and how they cut interruptions by 99 percent to keep over 85 percent useful training time.

candidates.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
candidates.why: What OpenAI's proof that the zeta zeros lie between 1/12 and 11/12 actually shows, which overlooked tools it combined, and how leading number theorists judge its correctness and its significance.

candidates.title: Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins
candidates.why: A lab's first-hand account of a model solving a 28-year-old cryptography mystery: how it guessed a 1990s random-number generator, spotted the statistical fingerprint, and recovered the generator states with lattice reduction.

candidates.title: How do Chinese AI companies make money?
candidates.why: A line-by-line look at the revenue of Alibaba, ByteDance, Z.ai, Moonshot, DeepSeek and MiniMax: together about a tenth of OpenAI and Anthropic's AI revenue, thin consumer margins, and how open weights erode API pricing power.

candidates.title: The AI buildout rests on hidden debt
candidates.why: How data centres are financed off balance sheet through special-purpose vehicles and private credit, and how banks pass the risk on, which is the mechanism behind this week's doubts about AI infrastructure valuations.
